service_preparing: The SPHEREx sky explorer is being prepared.
webgl_unavailable: WebGL2 is unavailable. Try a browser with hardware acceleration.
search_sky: Search the sky — a star, a comet, or coordinates
diff_unavailable: Diff λ unavailable: fewer than three reference frames at this wavelength.
diff_detector: Diff λ is precomputed in the default detector.
reference_caption: Precomputed, deblended target spectrum; not a measurement of the selected pixel.
credits: SPHEREx data: NASA / JPL-Caltech / IRSA. Astrometry: ESA Gaia DR3.
whole_stack: One stretch for the whole stack · 0.5–99.5 percentiles
no_gaia_target: No Gaia counterpart with measured proper motion is available for this target.
spectrum_pending: Select a sky position to measure its spectrum.
no_target: Select one of the five fields below.
same_stretch: The brightness scale stays fixed as the date changes.
blink_explain: Compare survey passes. The cross follows the catalogued position at each date.
diff_explain: A reference matched in wavelength separates changes from the detector’s color gradient.
barnard_intro: A nearby star crossing the background sky. Compare the earliest and latest survey passes.
eps_indi_b_intro: An unresolved pair of brown dwarfs, with methane absorption in the reference spectrum.
wise_0855_intro: The coldest known brown dwarf. In D1–D3 only a background star is visible.
rw_aur_intro: A young variable star and its dusty disk change differently across infrared wavelengths.
r_dra_intro: A Mira variable seen over repeated visits. Each detector has its own date coverage.
note_barnard_caveat: formal error ±{v0}″/yr; ±{v1} reflects frame systematics (saturated core, {v2} useful visits)
note_eps_indi_b_plx_ref: Gaia DR{v0} {v1} mas (ε Ind A: {v2} mas)
note_eps_indi_b_caveat: error from per-visit bootstrap ({v0} visits); dropping one control star gives {v1}–{v2} mas
note_wise_0855_w2_ref: published W{v0} ≈ {v1} mag ({v2} mJy); CatWISE{v3} {v4} ({v5} mJy)
note_wise_0855_caveat: {v0}% of the W{v1} band lies beyond SPHEREx's {v2} µm limit; the AllWISE catalogue value ({v3} mag, {v4} mJy) is blended at the {v5} position
note_r_dra_caveat: only {v0} cycles observed: consistent with the catalogued period, not an independent measurement ({v1}–{v2} µm gives {v3} d, {v4}–{v5})
free_caveat: Each spectral point is a forced ePSF measurement; unavailable exposures are reported separately.
moving_interval: Moving targets require an observing interval. Open their comet page to follow the spacecraft ephemeris.
resolve_unavailable: Object not resolved — check the name or coordinates.
explorer_description: Compare real SPHEREx survey images across dates and infrared wavelengths.
aladin_unavailable: Aladin reference unavailable — reopen Lab to retry.
hips_blank_channel: This dichroic channel is blank in the published HiPS.
hips_reference_note: The all-sky HiPS is a survey reference, not this exposure. Gaia positions here use the catalogue epoch.
flags_note: Flag highlights only affect the display. Live photometry applies the official mask.
jpl_geocentric: Geocentric positions are approximate markers, not spacecraft positions for photometry.
neo_intro: Thermal sizes after NEOWISE. Every estimate keeps its uncertainty, evidence tier and observing limits attached.
neo_counts: {a} tier A · {b} tier B · {p} provisional · {pha} potentially hazardous in A/B
neo_validation_plot: SPHEREx versus NEOWISE diameters, logarithmic axes
neo_validation_summary: Out-of-sample dispersion: −{lower}%/+{upper}% across {n} NEOWISE objects. The fitted median is not an accuracy measure.
neo_validation_missing: Absolute reference diameters are retained for {available} of {total} validation objects. The plot shows only those pairs; all published validation ratios remain available below. Full reference retrieval is pending.
neo_method_text: {model}. η = {eta} ± {sigma}; only trails ≤ {trail} px. Diameters and intervals are the published results, not fits made by this page. The systematic floor is additional to the tabulated interval. Albedo depends on H and the thermal diameter.
neo_single_note: A single visit does not measure rotational variability. Treat its size as preliminary.
neo_low_albedo: Very low inferred albedo: check H; the thermal diameter does not depend on H.
neo_selection: Select an object to inspect its retained photometry.
neo_view_sky: Open this observation in the sky explorer
neo_plot_note: Vertical bars: published 16–84% intervals. Open points: provisional. Reference curves assume the labelled albedos; they are not measurements.
comets_intro: A census of CO₂ released by comets, measured in SPHEREx frames. Each point is one comet at the epoch of its census, with the 16–84% range of the production rate Q.
comets_counts: {n} comets · {detected} detected · {systematics} with systematics · {marginal} marginal · {none} not detected
comets_chart_alt: Scatter plot of CO₂ production rate against heliocentric distance for {n} comets, log scales, with 16–84% bars
comets_honesty_census: This is a census by pass, not a real-time monitor: SPHEREx revisits each comet only a few times a year, and public data lag by weeks.
comets_honesty_velocity: Q is proportional to the outflow speed. Assuming a speed of 0.50 instead of 0.85 r_h^−0.5 km/s lowers every Q by about {percent}%: treat this as a systematic on top of the plotted range.
comets_honesty_far: Beyond {au} au the band flux is too small for a trustworthy Q. Those points are marked and should not be interpreted.
comets_honesty_systematics: “With systematics” means a band is present (S/N ≥ 5) but the band model fits poorly (χ²ᵣ ≥ 50): the Q shown is not trusted at its quoted precision.
comets_pick: Select a point or a row to see its numbers.
comets_detail_q: Q(CO₂) {q50} [{q16}–{q84}] s⁻¹; alternative recipes: {alt_tau} (τ, g) and {alt_v} (speed).
comets_detail_diag: S/N {snr}; σ_F/F {err}; {core} core channels; χ²ᵣ {chi2}; T_rot {t} K.
comets_validation_intro: Two results are compared with published values. A measurement that falls inside the published range is consistent with it; it is not an independent confirmation.
comets_val_interval_source: 16–84% interval from the research notes, not re-run in this build.
comets_val_pending: Pending: 3I/ATLAS H₂O in August 2025 is not shown. {reason}
comets_method_text: CO₂ ν₃ band model with P and R branches over a sky-subtracted spectrum; Q from a Haser parent model with a Monte Carlo over flux, calibration, g-factor, lifetime and speed. Detection requires S/N ≥ 5 and χ²ᵣ < 50. Percentiles are 16/50/84.
comets_credits: SPHEREx: NASA/JPL-Caltech/IRSA · Published values as cited in each row
comets_open_sky: Open this comet in the Explorer
cd_plate: Real SPHEREx frames, centred on the comet
cd_plate_note: Each frame is one exposure at one wavelength, tracked on the comet with the JPL Horizons ephemeris and shown with the stack's common stretch. No continuum is subtracted and no gas map is made: where the CO₂ band is bright you see it as a brighter, larger coma only in the frames marked “in band”.
cd_plate_alt: SPHEREx frame of {name} at {lam} µm on {date}, north up
cd_spectrum_d5_note: D5, sky subtracted, 3 px aperture, window 3.85–4.42 µm. One point per exposure.
cd_spectrum_d6_note: D6 spectrum used for the CO census; the CO (1–0) band sits at 4.55–4.80 µm.
cd_q_alt: Alternative recipes: {alt_tau} with other τ and g; {alt_v} with a lower outflow speed.
cd_diag_line: S/N {snr} · σ_F/F {err} · {core} core channels · χ²ᵣ {chi2} · T_rot {t} K · r_h {r} au · Δ {delta} au
cd_aperture: Q against aperture: {q2} (2 px), {q3} (3 px), {q5} (5 px), {q8} (8 px) s⁻¹. A strong trend means the gas is not a simple parent-molecule coma.
cd_prov_track: Tracked with JPL Horizons target {track}, observer SPHEREx.
cd_prov_stack: Stack {epoch} · D{det} · {n} frames · {shown} shown (≥ 95% valid pixels)
cd_29p_note: 29P is a centaur-like comet that is active far from the Sun: its CO₂ census value comes from a single visit sweep in December 2025.
cd_3i_note_aug: August 2025: the epoch behind the validated CO₂ figure.
cd_3i_note_dec: December 2025: a band is present but the model fits poorly, so Q is not trusted at its quoted precision.
